questions.text: Quick Revision - Definition of Chemical Reaction

definitionBean.title: Definition of Chemical Reaction
definitionBean.definition: The process in which one or more substances combine to form new substances with distinct properties is called a chemical reaction.
definitionBean.explanation: During a chemical reaction, old chemical bonds break and new chemical bonds are formed, yielding substances with completely new properties.
importantPoints: It cannot be reversed by physical methods

definitionBean.title: Reactants and Products
definitionBean.definition: Substances that take part in a chemical reaction are called 'reactants' and new substances formed as a result of the reaction are called 'products'.
definitionBean.explanation: When writing equations, reactants are shown on the left-hand side (LHS) and products on the right-hand side (RHS) connected by an arrow.
importantPoints: Reactants: Those that take part in the reaction
Products: Those formed after the reaction
Arrow sign ($\rightarrow$) indicates the direction of the reaction

questions.text: Quick Revision - Signs of Chemical Reaction (Color Change and Gas)

definitionBean.title: Signs of Chemical Reaction
definitionBean.definition: The occurrence of a chemical reaction is identified by change in state, change in color, evolution of gas, or temperature change.
definitionBean.explanation: During a reaction, substances often change color or release various gases, confirming that a reaction has taken place.

questions.text: Subject: Definition of Chemical Reaction and Reactants-Products

parts.statement: What is a chemical reaction? Explain with the example of magnesium ribbon combustion.
parts.correct_answer: Formation of substances with new properties is a chemical reaction; burning magnesium forms magnesium oxide.
parts.explanation: The process in which substances with new properties are formed is called a chemical reaction. When a magnesium ribbon is burned in air, it reacts with oxygen to form a white powder (magnesium oxide).

parts.statement: What do reactants and products mean? Clarify through a chemical equation.
parts.correct_answer: Participants are reactants and formed substances are products.
parts.explanation: Substances taking part in a reaction are 'reactants' and the new substances formed are 'products'. Example: In $\text{Zn} + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow \text{ZnSO}_4 + \text{H}_2$, zinc and sulfuric acid are reactants while zinc sulfate and hydrogen are products.

questions.text: Subject: Signs of Chemical Reaction (Color Change and Gas Evolution)

parts.statement: Explain color change in chemical reactions with an example.
parts.correct_answer: Blue color of copper sulfate turns green upon adding an iron nail.
parts.explanation: When an iron nail is dipped into a blue solution of copper sulfate, the blue color of the solution changes to light green (due to the formation of iron sulfate).

parts.statement: Which gas is evolved when zinc reacts with dilute sulfuric acid? How will you test it?
parts.correct_answer: Hydrogen gas is evolved which burns with a pop sound.
parts.explanation: Hydrogen gas ($\text{H}_2$) is evolved in this reaction. When a burning matchstick is brought near it, it burns with a 'pop' sound.

questions.text: Subject: Signs of Chemical Reaction (Temperature Change and Precipitation)

parts.statement: How is change in temperature an indicator of a chemical reaction? Give an example.
parts.correct_answer: Exothermic or endothermic reactions cause changes in temperature.
parts.explanation: In some chemical reactions, heat is released (exothermic), increasing the temperature, such as adding water to quicklime. In others, heat is absorbed (endothermic), decreasing the temperature.

parts.statement: What is meant by the formation of a precipitate? Give a suitable example.
parts.correct_answer: Separation of an insoluble solid is called a precipitate.
parts.explanation: The separation of an insoluble solid substance during a chemical reaction is called a 'precipitate'. Example: Reaction of potassium iodide and lead nitrate forms a yellow precipitate of lead iodide.
